title: Parts of a Garment
summary: Students build from Week 3 garment names into garment-part vocabulary and detail-focused description. They identify visible parts on garments, label details on images, understand short spoken and written detail descriptions, practice A2 phrase frames such as It has and There is or There are, and produce a scaffolded Garment Details Card.
essential_question: How can I identify and explain visible garment parts in simple English for Fashion Design study?
professional_context: Week 4 connects English to the visible details Fashion Design students notice in drawing, sewing, patternmaking, garment observation, technical description, and simple critique. Students need this language to label what they see and explain where a detail is and why it matters.
grammar_focus: There is a ___ on the front
teacher_preparation: Preview the Week 4 garment-detail overview board, the two vocabulary boards, the labeled garment image, and the listening script before class.
Prepare visible sentence frames for It has, They have, There is, There are, on the front, on the back, at the top, at the bottom, and near the hem.
Review the Week 4 correction targets, especially missing articles, singular and plural detail nouns, and on versus at in location phrases.
Decide whether students will build the Garment Details Card from a projected garment gallery, printed cards, or a future app gallery.
Bring or project garment-detail image cards for the teacher-led pronunciation, labeling warm-up, and speaking session.
student_deliverables: Completion of the Week 4 opener and detail-recognition task.
Completion of the main garment-parts vocabulary matching sets.
Reading and visual-labeling responses about one garment image.
Listening-comprehension responses identifying garments, details, and locations from short spoken descriptions.
Completion of phrase-practice items using It has, There is, There are, and location phrases.
A scaffolded Garment Details Card with 5 to 6 required sentence-frame lines and one optional challenge line.
One corrected Week 4 sentence saved after review.
A short teacher-observed oral explanation of one garment and its visible details.
